long_biography.plain_text:
After graduating from Menlo College, Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal returned to Saudi Arabia and began building a business with family-provided seed capital and a mortgaged house. Early real-estate and contracting activity supplied a base for larger investments, while a successful takeover of United Saudi Commercial Bank broadened his reach into finance.

His defining international move came during Citicorp’s early-1990s crisis, when he invested heavily in the struggling bank. The recovery established his reputation for buying valuable assets under pressure and helped finance a wider portfolio through Kingdom Holding Company. Hotels, media, technology and real estate followed, but disciplined capital allocation—not a government office or state-owned petroleum asset—remained the private fortune’s central mechanism.
